statement: Narrowing an over-broad rule can turn what it caught by accident into false claims. Cejel #533 read a shell conditional only as a command's first word, so `npm test` no longer hid `npm ci`. But the old any-word rule had also been the only thing withholding guards behind `(`, `{` or `!`, so `( [ -n "$X" ] && npm ci )` became a false "CI requires a lockfile" claim, and v27 scored it 0. The same PR called its workflow reader linear after timing flat steps only; nested items cost depth times size. It also decided which directories the checkout holds by lstat on the scanning host, so a symlink, a case-insensitive volume or an empty untracked directory changed the certificate. Rules: before narrowing a rule, list what it caught incidentally and keep catching it; time the deepest nesting, not only the longest input; decide facts about the checkout from the inventory the scan binds, never from the host.
